Mulberry Schools Trust
Executive Headteacher’s Message
At Mulberry Stepney Green Maths, Computing & Science College our vision is to ensure that all our students have the opportunity to gain the qualifications and skills required for them to take their rightful place in a global community.
To us, every child matters and we work together with our families to realise our students’ dreams and aspirations. At Mulberry Stepney Green there is a real drive for academic excellence, coupled with an approach to develop the whole person, making learning enjoyable and exciting.
Principal’s Message
At Mulberry Stepney Green, we believe in the power of aspirations. We encourage our students to dream big, set ambitious goals and actively engage with everything the school has to offer.
Our community is one where every individual is supported in their journey to success, with staff, students and parents working together to unlock each student’s full potential. Here, lasting friendships are formed and a sense of belonging is nurtured in a positive, inclusive environment.

POST 16 ADMISSIONS POLICY
Mulberry Stepney Green Sixth Form gives priority to students from Mulberry Stepney Green Maths, Computing & Science College but accepts student applications from other schools.
General arrangements and entry requirements
Mulberry Stepney Green Maths, Computing & Science College provides a full programme of study. Students are considered for entry provided they meet the course entry requirements. The individual subjects have their own specific criteria and students suitability for courses is decided at an admissions meeting with school staff. Students who do not fulfil the entry criteria for the chosen courses or subjects, or whose chosen post 16 pathway or course, cannot be accommodated by the school, are guided onto the most appropriate alternative courses or subjects.
All students are required to sign a learning agreement that outlines the commitment expected for successful study at post 16. Parents are also asked to sign the learning agreement.
Availability of places
There is capacity for a maximum total of 340 students in years 12 and 13, including external candidates. The number of places available to students is determined by taking into account the following:
Availability of accommodation
Availability of teaching and other resources
Capacity of individual courses
Curriculum balance across the School
Applying for entry
Applications to Mulberry Stepney Green Maths, Computing & Science College must be made on the school’s application form and forwarded to the school. For external applicants this should be to the Head of Sixth Form.

A-Level Sports Science
The course will provide the opportunity to take students knowledge and understanding of Physical Education and the World of Sport to an advanced level. Following on from the GCSE PE course the A level allows students to advance their theoretical knowledge and understanding whilst specialising in a specific range of sports in a choice of roles. Success in this course will provide a clear link to studying a Sport related course in Higher Education. Choices could include Sports Science, Sports Psychologist, Elite coach or PE teacher.
For full details of the course Specification go to edexcel.com
OCR GCE A Level in Physical Education (H555)
OCR’s A Level PE (H555) comprises three assessed theoretical components and a non-exam assessment (NEA) component. Component 1 focuses on Physiological Factors Affecting Performance, Component 2 on Psychological Factors Affecting Performance, and Component 3 on Socio-Cultural Issues in Physical Activity and Sport. The NEA, broken into two parts (performance and Evaluating and Analysing Performance for Improvement), assesses practical application.
Course Outline
The OCR A-Level PE course outline covers applied anatomy and physiology, exercise physiology, biomechanics, skill acquisition, sports psychology, sport and society, and contemporary issues in sport. The course blends theoretical content with practical elements, allowing students to improve their own performance or coaching skills and gain a deeper understanding of sports science, coaching, and the socio-cultural aspects of physical activity.

French and Spanish
Faculty of:
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
Head of Faculty:
About the department:
The Modern Foreign Languages Faculty consists of 5 teaching staff. French or Spanish is taught to all Year 7 pupils for 3 lessons a week and in year 8 students choose to continue with the same subject or choose Bengali. The Faculty occupies 5 classrooms in the new building and two conference rooms which are suitable for conversation classes with small groups of students. All classrooms are equipped with interactive whiteboards and sound. Additionally, one of the classrooms is equipped with 30 network computer stations.
Key stage 3 Curriculum:
KS3 is well-resourced, using Studio 1-2 to support the French curriculum and Viva 1-2 to support the Spanish curriculum. We create most of our own resources, and have access to many online resources.

Key stage 4 Curriculum:
In year 9 students follow the KS3 national curriculum as well as studying 3 topics related to the GCSE course. In year 10 and 11 the exam board used is AQA GCSE French Full Course (8658) and Spanish Full Course (8698). The Final Assessment consists of 4 test papers: Listening, Reading, Speaking & Writing which are taken in the final term of year 11. Studio AQA GCSE is used to support the GCSE French learning and Viva AQA GCSE for the Spanish. In GCSE French and Spanish students study the following areas:
Theme 1 – Identity and Culture

Discussing plans for the future
Extra-Curricular:
The department offers many extra-curricular opportunities to the students. Pupils studying Spanish have had the opportunity to spend a week in the Barcelona region taking part in cultural visits and those studying French can visit Paris for 4 days. Also Year 7 pupils spend a day in Boulogne in the summer term. In addition, this year the faculty is planning to take KS4 pupils to subject specific conferences. This year the faculty is also planning a cross-curricular G and T visit to the Wallace Collection. The department also offers booster sessions for year 11 at lunch during the spring term and regular school holidays intervention during half terms. Yr12 also have the opportunity to study French at AS and A level as part of the enrichment programme in the VIth form.

Principal and Executive Headteacher’s Message
Mr Z. Chowdhury
At Mulberry Stepney Green, we believe in the power of aspirations. We encourage our students to dream big, set ambitious goals and actively engage with everything the school has to offer.
Our community is one where every individual is supported in their journey to success, with staff, students and parents working together to unlock each student’s full potential. Here, lasting friendships are formed and a sense of belonging is nurtured in a positive, inclusive environment.
We are deeply committed to innovation and preparing our students for the challenges and opportunities of the future. We don’t just focus on academic achievement; we aim to inspire curiosity, creativity and a sense of responsibility.
Our students leave equipped not just with qualifications, but with the mindset to lead, make a difference, and keep learning for life.
As we look to the future, we are driven by a vision of continued progress and ambition. We are committed to expanding opportunities for our students both in and outside the classroom, ensuring they develop the confidence, independence, and compassion to be leaders and changemakers. Our strategic goals reflect this commitment, focusing on developing a school that empowers our students and strengthens our community.
Principal Mr Z. Chowdhury
At Mulberry Stepney Green Maths, Computing & Science College our vision is to ensure that all our students have the opportunity to gain the qualifications and skills required for them to take their rightful place in a global community.
To us, every child matters and we work together with our families to realise our students’ dreams and aspirations.
At Mulberry Stepney Green there is a real drive for academic excellence, coupled with an approach to develop the whole person, making learning enjoyable and exciting.
We hope that you enjoy browsing and interacting with the information on this website, resulting in you wanting to contact us and find out more about Mulberry Stepney Green Maths, Computing & Science College. We look forward to meeting you.

PSHE & Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE)
PSHE and RSHE is an important part of our curriculum. It helps students stay safe, build positive relationships, and develop the knowledge and skills they need for life. Our approach is age-appropriate, inclusive and focused on supporting students’ wellbeing.
Why we teach PSHE and RSHE
At our school, PSHE and Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) are an important part of helping students develop the knowledge and skills they need to stay safe, healthy and prepared for life.

The world our young people are growing up in is changing rapidly, particularly with the influence of social media and online life. The updated national guidance reflects this and ensures that teaching remains relevant, age-appropriate and focused on keeping students safe.
PSHE and RSHE are delivered in a way that is:
We aim to work in partnership with parents and carers so that students receive consistent, supportive messages both at school and at home.
Lessons are carefully planned to be appropriate for students’ age and development. Staff create a safe, respectful environment where students can ask questions and explore topics with support.
We recognise that families and relationships can look different for everyone. Our curriculum reflects this diversity and promotes respect for all.
Parents have the right to request withdrawal from some aspects of sex education (but not relationships or health education). Please contact the school for further information.
